title: allocator fragmentation batching starvation handoff
content:
Summary:

This is a working incident-handoff and runbook draft for an on-call series where we observed repeated OOMs and sustained microbatch starvation on a subset of serving hosts. Root cause hypothesis: allocator fragmentation combined with bursty continuous-batching growth + pinned KV-cache shards caused inability to allocate large contiguous blocks for prefetch/batch assembly, which in turn caused the batching loop to stall and trigger cascading requests and memory pressure until OOMs.

Scope/Impact:
- Affected pool: rwd-serving-gpu-pool-6 (NVIDIA A100s)
- Time window: 2025-10-31 03:20 -> 2025-10-31 05:45 UTC (recurring small spikes the next day)
- Symptoms: increased tail latency for generation endpoints, sporadic 502s, and process OOM kills on ~12 hosts (out of 140 in pool).
- Customer-visible: degradation on internal canary traffic and two paying customers with low traffic but strict SLOs. No data loss reported; requests retried.

Quick tl;dr for next on-call:
- If you see the same pattern (batch loops blocked, gradual resident set growth, large free-space fragmentation): perform the rapid-mitigation steps (rolling drain + host restart OR reduce continuous-batch max_tokens to 128 for the affected model priority).
- Prioritize contacting serving-runtime on-call and the allocator owners (see linked PR).

Observed indicators (what to look for):
- Metrics: sudden divergence between total_allocated_bytes and usable_contiguous_free_bytes (we don't have a single metric yet, see PromQL below).
- Logs: repeated "failed allocate contiguous region: requested=XXMB available-chunk=YYMB" messages in runtime logs (example excerpt below).
- Kernel/system: dmesg shows process OOM kills with 'cudaMalloc' failing; nvidia-smi shows high memory utilization but with small free ranges.

Example log excerpt (scrubbed):
[2025-10-31T03:41:12Z] serving-runtime[batcher.cpp:442] WARN batch-assembler: contiguous-alloc-fail req=134217728 avail-largest=50331648 (model=llama-30b-quant)
[2025-10-31T03:41:12Z] serving-runtime[allocator.cpp:301] ERROR allocator: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory, requested=134217728
[2025-10-31T03:41:13Z] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 21234 (serving-runtime) score 327

Hypothesis details (why fragmentation?):
- Continuous batching requests create large transient buffers for KV cache + attention scratch + prefix caching.
- KV-cache pinning (shard-aligned allocations) caused many medium-sized allocations that persisted (hot keys).
- Over time, freed transient allocations left small holes; jemalloc-like allocator we use doesn't coalesce because of pinned fragmentation semantics on GPU-backed allocator path.
- When a large batch assembly needs one contiguous block, the allocator cannot satisfy it though total free memory > request size. This triggers fallback allocations, additional retries, and eventual OOM when several such events coincide.

Repro steps (dev/debug):
1) Reproduce in staging using the continuous-batcher load generator: run loadgen with variable seq_len (50% sequences with 1024 tokens) and KV-cache enabled.
2) Enable jemalloc stats and our allocator debug (ENV: RWD_ALLOC_DEBUG=1) to dump free-chunk histogram periodically.
3) Observe if the "largest_free_chunk" metric trends down while total_free stays high.

PromQL ideas (quick dashboards to add to OnCall):
- sum(rate(serving_runtime_batch_failures_total[5m])) by (host,model)
- max_over_time(allocator_largest_free_chunk_bytes[10m]) < 20000000 and node_gpu_mem_free_bytes > 200000000 -> sign of fragmentation
- increase(process_resident_memory_bytes[10m]) > 200MB per host -> chase allocation growth

Immediate mitigation steps (fast, risk-graded):
1) Safe quick: Handoff to SRE and initiate rolling drain of affected hosts (kubectl cordon && drain with --ignore-daemonsets) then restart serving-runtime process. This frees pinned shards and compacts allocator state.
2) Faster, less disruptive: PATCH the runtime to force the batcher to prefer smaller per-request contiguous allocations: set CONT_BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=128 for the affected model group via runtime config API (Console -> model routes).
3) Emergency fallback: disable prefetch for high-memory models (toggle route prefetch=false) to reduce transient allocation pressure.
4) If multiple hosts are failing at once and draining isn't keeping up: scale up Dedicated capacity or fallback to a lower-capacity compatible variant (e.g., llama-30b-quant -> llama-13b-quant) via routing policy.

On-call triage checklist (step-by-step):
- [ ] Confirm alerts: check pager or Datadog alert linked to batch-failure/oom count.
- [ ] Identify affected hosts: query serving_runtime_process_oom_total{pool="rwd-serving-gpu-pool-6"}.
- [ ] SSH to an affected host (if allowed) and run: nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY; sudo cat /proc/<pid>/maps | grep -i heap; journalctl -u serving-runtime -n 200.
- [ ] Check allocator debug endpoint: curl http://localhost:11223/allocator/debug -> copy largest_free_chunk histogram.
- [ ] If histogram largest_free_chunk < 64MB and queued batch requests > 10: enact mitigation (reduce CONT_BATCH_MAX_TOKENS or drain).

Longer-term mitigations & action items (owners assigned):
- Add a metric for allocator_largest_free_chunk_bytes (Action: June Park, eng-platform) - due 2025-12-01.
- Implement an allocator compaction pass or use a different GPU allocation strategy that supports coalescing (Action: Carlos Ortega, serving-runtime) - RFC due 2026-01-10.
- Add automated runbook play in Console: when fragmentation flag triggers, auto-scale dedicated reserve by 10% while alerting (Action: Priya Mehta + Product) - POC due 2026-02-01.
- Postmortem writeup and customer outreach draft (Action: SRE lead) - include timeline + mitigations.

Open threads/questions to resolve:
- Does the CUDA driver or our GPU allocator provide a way to defragment without full restart? (asked in PR comment)
- Are there models/routes that routinely pin shard-aligned allocations unnecessarily? Need audit across model catalog.
- Can the batcher be more resilient by allocating in smaller contiguous chunks and stitching? Tradeoffs for perf/cost need evaluation.

Notes to self / on-call handoff tips:
- This incident behaves like a "slow boil" — not a single burst. Look for incremental loss of large free chunks across hours.
- Avoid large-scale immediate config flips across the fleet; limit changes to the affected pool and monitor for regression.
- Keep communication in #sre and notify #serving-runtime; link the JIRA (INF-2345) in messages.

References & artifacts:
- JIRA INF-2345 (root cause/coordination issue)
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4821 (allocator debug helpers)
- Slack: #sre thread (ts:2025-10-31_03:50) and #serving-runtime discussion
- Console route: /models/llama-30b-quant -> current batcher config (snapshot attached in Confluence)

Appendix: useful commands for triage (copy/paste)
- kubectl get pods -n serving -l pool=rwd-serving-gpu-pool-6 -o wide
- kubectl exec -it <pod> -- curl http://127.0.0.1:11223/allocator/debug
- nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY; nvidia-smi topo -m
- sudo journalctl -u serving-runtime -o short-iso --since "2025-10-31 03:00" | grep -i "alloc" -n

If you're the next on-call and want context, ping me (Priya) on Slack; I have the staging repro and memory histograms. This doc is a handoff — treat as living draft.

-- end of handoff draft --
